title: Verifier-Gated LLM NetOps: A Preregistered, Artifact-Backed Evaluation of Input-Sanitization and Deterministic Verification Against Adversarial Intents
abstract: We report a preregistered paired confirmatory experiment (study_id cand-2026-03) that measured whether template-based input sanitization combined with deterministic verifier-gating (plus at-most-one automated repair) changes the rate at which a deterministic validator accepts LLM-generated CLI configurations under adversarially mutated intents. The frozen run used gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 within an orchestrated generate–validate–repair adapter. Planned episodes = 300; completed episodes = 282; complete paired outcomes used in the primary analysis = 141. Observed per-pair acceptance: Baseline 135/141 (95.74468085%); Guarded 141/141 (100.0%); paired absolute difference = 0.04255319148936165; exact two-sided McNemar p = 0.03125; 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.014184397163120567, 0.07801418439716312]. We disclose a protocol deviation (unset runtime sampling temperature) and that the preregistered benign-control (M = 50) was not executed; interpretations are therefore explicitly bounded to the archived synthetic task bank and the formal estimand of validator acceptance. All principal numeric claims are supported by the archived execution and analysis artifacts referenced in Methods and Results.

sections.introduction: Automating intent-to-configuration translation with large language models (LLMs) promises operational efficiencies for network operations (NetOps), but unsafe or semantically incorrect outputs create deployment risks. Deterministic network verifiers can gate deployment by checking semantics (ordering, invariants, protected fields) rather than token-level similarity; combine that with input sanitization and bounded automated repair and one obtains a practical generate–validate–repair architecture for LLM-assisted NetOps. Prior work documents LLM failure modes for configuration generation and prototype improvements from verifier-assisted repair, but evaluations frequently report token- or reference-level metrics that do not measure validator-acceptance/deployability directly [3,8,9]. We therefore posed a narrowly scoped, preregistered question that is operationally meaningful and experimentally tractable: How effective are template-based input sanitization and deterministic verifier-gating (with at-most-one automated repair) at changing the rate at which a deterministic validator accepts LLM-generated CLI configurations when inputs are adversarially mutated? Contributions. (1) A preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment (cand-2026-03) that isolates downstream guarded-pipeline effects under shared_initial_candidate semantics; (2) a formal, artifact-grounded estimand and confirmatory test using deterministic validator acceptance as the primary quantity of interest; (3) concrete, reproducible quantitative outcomes from the archived run; and (4) an explicit reconciliation of preregistration wording, an identified protocol deviation (unset sampling temperature), and practical recommendations for reproducible follow-up studies.
sections.related_work: Deterministic verification tools (Header Space Analysis, VeriFlow, NetPlumber family) are established methods for checking forwarding, access-control and sequencing invariants and thus provide semantics-focused acceptance criteria suitable as deployment gates [5–7]. Empirical studies of LLMs for NetOps (e.g., NetConfEval, NetLLMBench, and zero-touch proposals) consistently report that model-only generation produces both syntactic and higher-level semantic errors, motivating verifier-based gating and repair [3,8,9]. Generate–validate–repair architectures and tool-oriented orchestration (Toolformer-like patterns) have been demonstrated to improve narrow-task outcomes when verifier diagnostics are actionable and repair scope is constrained [11,3]. The security literature documents prompt-injection and indirect-prompt attacks that can subvert LLM-integrated pipelines, motivating input sanitization and gate designs in NetOps contexts [10]. Surveys of AIOps/telecommunications highlight fragmented evaluation practices and call for validator-centered deployability metrics; our work directly measures validator acceptance as the primary operational quantity [4,9].
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The study cand-2026-03 was preregistered prior to observing outcomes (preregistration_sha256: ba6ed25e84c7240fbe94f2d50b3e778fbfffd810ff2db632df8946e85f0f1373). The primary estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline: per adversarial intent, outcome = 1 if the deterministic validator would accept the final candidate for deployment, 0 otherwise. Confirmatory inference used an exact two-sided McNemar on paired outcomes; bootstrap percentile 95% CIs used 10,000 resamples with seed = 1729.

Design, tasks and adversary. The preregistered design targeted N = 150 adversarial intents with paired runs (Baseline vs Guarded), implemented as mutations of synthetic intent templates that exercise interface admin changes, MTU and VLAN updates, sequencing constraints, and protected-interface rules. The adversary model applied deterministic mutation heuristics (string-level, token insertion, slot-override classes) to those templates. Scope is explicitly limited to the synthetic intent bank and the deterministic CLI grammar encoded in the validator; no production operator logs or private datasets were used.

Model, validator and pipeline semantics. The declared generator was gpt-5-mini and the deterministic validator deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Orchestration used a generate–validate–repair adapter implementing shared_initial_candidate semantics: a single LLM generation per intent was produced and reused for both Baseline and Guarded branches so that any paired difference can arise only from downstream sanitization, gating, and permitted repair (no independent initial-generation variance). The guarded branch applied a template-based input sanitizer, deterministically blocked candidates that failed explicit safety checks, and—where policy permitted—invoked at most one automated repair LLM call; the repair policy was bounded as preregistered.

Missingness, exclusions and protocol deviation. The preregistration specified excluding a paired unit only when both paired runs were technical failures (model/API failure, verifier timeout, or parser error). The archived run recorded completed_episodes = 282 and failed_episodes = 18; after applying the preregistered exclusion rule 141 complete pairs entered the primary analysis. We disclose a protocol deviation: execution/model_configuration.json recorded an unset runtime sampling temperature (temperature = null). To preserve paired comparability the pipeline used shared_initial_candidate semantics; for deterministic reproduction we recommend explicitly setting temperature = 0 and re-running with the archived task manifest and execution manifest. The preregistered benign-control (M = 50) and the false-positive-blocking secondary estimand were not executed in this run; consequently no empirical false-positive-blocking rates are reported here and interpretations that would require those results are limited accordingly.
sections.results:
Execution summary and sample accounting. Planned episodes = 300; completed = 282; failed = 18; complete paired outcomes for primary analysis = 141 after applying the preregistered exclusion rule. Provider-call accounting in the archived run shows hosted_model_call_event_count = 156 (completed = 147, failed = 9), with stage_counts reporting 150 shared_initial_generation events and 6 repair-stage events.

Condition-level outcomes and paired inference. Condition summary (complete_pairs = 141) reports baseline_successes = 135 (baseline success rate = 0.9574468085106383) and guarded_successes = 141 (guarded success rate = 1.0). The paired contingency table is n11 = 135, n10 = 6, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. The preregistered exact two-sided McNemar on these paired outcomes yields p = 0.03125. The observed paired point estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.04255319148936165; the 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) is [0.014184397163120567, 0.07801418439716312]. All these numbers are archived in the execution and analysis artifacts cited below.

Discordant-case diagnostics and repairs. The six discordant pairs (n10) are traceable in the archived per-episode validator traces and are associated with the guarded pipeline converting an initial draft that the validator would have rejected into a final candidate the validator accepted. Provider-call accounting links repair-stage activity to these discordant pairs: stage_counts.repair = 6. For those six episodes the guarded path produced acceptance via sanitizer normalization and/or a single permitted automated repair whose output satisfied the deterministic validator. Because the formal estimand measures validator acceptance-for-deployment, such repair-enabled conversions increase guarded acceptance even when they recover benign-but-malformed drafts rather than directly neutralizing an adversary advantage.

Missingness sensitivity. Nine paired units were excluded because both runs failed technically. As a conservative sensitivity check (not the primary preregistered analysis), treating those excluded pairs as failures yields baseline acceptance = 135/150 = 0.9000 and guarded acceptance = 141/150 = 0.9400; this preserves the direction of the observed paired difference but reduces overall rates and effective sample size.

Unexecuted preregistered analyses. The preregistered benign-control (M = 50) and the false-positive-blocking secondary estimand were not executed; therefore no empirical false-positive-blocking claims are advanced here. This omission constrains operational conclusions about sanitizer-induced benign rejections and is explicitly acknowledged in Methods, Results and Discussion.
sections.discussion:
Interpretive boundary and practical significance. The archived confirmatory outcome shows a small but statistically detectable increase in deterministic-validator acceptance under the guarded pipeline (≈4.255 percentage points) driven by six discordant conversions associated with permitted repairs. Two caveats are essential. First, validator acceptance is a semantics-focused but partial proxy for operational safety: acceptance depends on the validator's encoded properties and does not guarantee absence of all protocol-level or runtime hazards. Second, the high baseline (ceiling effect) means a modest absolute change can be statistically detectable but of limited operational magnitude; the small discordant count (n10 = 6) underscores that practical impact should be judged case-by-case.

Operational implications and co-design. In synthetic scope, input sanitization plus bounded automated repair can reduce operator rework by converting invalid drafts into validator-accepted candidates; this is beneficial when repairs preserve intended semantics. Conversely, repairs that unintentionally mask adversarial manipulations could increase risk. Consequently, operational deployment should co-design gating policies, repair scope, and validator expressiveness: (a) require printers/diagnostics from verifiers that are actionable and machine-parsable; (b) bound automated repair attempts and log repair provenance for human audit; and (c) measure attacker-centric estimands that combine validator acceptance with independent semantic-safety checks.

Reproducibility and recommended fixes. To reproduce deterministic behavior we recommend setting provider sampling explicitly (temperature = 0) and re-running the archived task manifest with the declared model and validator. The archived execution and analysis manifests contain the machine-readable provenance and per-episode validator traces needed to reproduce the confirmatory numbers; practitioners should avoid relying on provider default sampling when paired comparability is required.

Threats to validity. Internal validity: technical failures (18/300 episodes) reduced sample size and led to preregistered exclusions. Construct validity: the deterministic validator encodes CLI grammar, sequencing and protected-field invariants but omits some dynamic protocol semantics; acceptance is therefore a partial proxy for deployability. External validity: single-model (gpt-5-mini), single-validator and synthetic task-bank limit generalization across vendors, CLI dialects, and production environments. Conclusion validity: small absolute effect on a high baseline requires cautious operational interpretation.
sections.conclusion: A preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment on a synthetic adversarial intent bank found that template-based input sanitization combined with deterministic verifier-gating and at-most-one automated repair produced a small but statistically detectable absolute increase in deterministic-validator-accepted LLM-generated configurations (paired difference ≈ 0.04255; p = 0.03125; 95% CI [0.01418, 0.07801]). Diagnostics show the discordant conversions were associated with permitted repair calls that enabled acceptance; this formal-estimand improvement does not equate to measured reduction in attacker success under attacker-centric definitions. Limitations include synthetic scope, single-model/validator evaluation, technical failures reducing sample size, and a protocol deviation (unset runtime temperature). Future work should execute the preregistered benign-control, measure attacker-centric estimands with an independent semantic-safety oracle, diversify models/validators across vendors and CLI dialects, and fix sampling settings (e.g., temperature = 0) for deterministic reproduction. All principal numbers above are supported by archived execution and analysis artifacts in the study's evidence bundle and manifests referenced below.

disclosure_statement: This study was executed autonomously after an autonomy lock under the archived master prompt (provenance/master_prompt.txt, SHA-256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Human role and autonomy boundary: a human Research Director selected the topic family (Generative AI / LLMs for NetOps) and constrained the initial master prompt prior to the autonomy lock; all literature review, preregistration, experiment design, code generation, experiment execution, analysis, peer-review cycles, manuscript drafting, and revision reported here were performed autonomously after the lock. Declared tools and orchestration: primary generator = gpt-5-mini; deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5; task generator = deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5; orchestration adapter family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Preregistration: study cand-2026-03 was preregistered and archived prior to observing outcomes (preregistration_sha256: ba6ed25e84c7240fbe94f2d50b3e778fbfffd810ff2db632df8946e85f0f1373). Protocol deviation: the archived run recorded an unset runtime sampling temperature (temperature = null); this is disclosed because provider-side defaults can affect sampling determinism. To preserve paired comparability the pipeline used shared_initial_candidate semantics (single shared generation per intent) and provider-call accounting in the archived manifests documents the actual call pattern. For deterministic reproduction we recommend explicitly setting temperature = 0 when re-running the archived task manifest. All execution and analysis artifacts (execution and analysis manifests, per-episode validator traces, and aggregated statistics) are archived in the study evidence bundle. No human manually edited or corrected the manuscript technical content after the autonomy lock.
limitations: Synthetic task bank and intent templates — not real production traffic or operator logs; results may not generalize to field datasets.
Single-model evaluation (gpt-5-mini) and single validator implementation limit external validity across vendors, protocols, and model families.
Validator coverage constrained to encoded safety properties (CLI grammar, required sequences, protected-interface invariants); some protocol-level or dynamic runtime semantics are not represented.
Technical failures (18/300 episodes) reduced effective sample size; paired exclusion (both-run failures = 9) was preregistered and applied.
Adversary model limited to deterministic mutations of synthetic intents; prompt-injection in retrieval-augmented or multi-source pipelines was not exhaustively evaluated.
A preregistration natural-language hypothesis phrasing differed from the registered formal estimand; results are reported and interpreted with respect to the archived formal estimand.
The preregistered benign-control (M = 50) and false-positive-blocking secondary estimand were not executed; therefore no empirical false-positive-blocking claims are made.
